summary: Isaiah described a Servant who would be rejected and would suffer for other people's sins. 'By His wounds we are healed.' Hundreds of years later, Jesus fulfilled this prophecy on the cross.

story_reel.narration: Isaiah also wrote about a mysterious person he called the Servant of Yahweh. But this Servant wouldn't look like a mighty king. Isaiah said, 'He was despised and rejected by people. He was a man of sorrows who knew what suffering was like. People turned their faces away from Him.' Why would God's chosen Servant suffer? Isaiah explained: 'Surely He carried our sadness and our pain. He was pierced for our wrongdoing. He was crushed for our sins. The punishment that brought us peace was on Him, and by His wounds we are healed.' Then Isaiah wrote, 'All of us, like sheep, have wandered away. Each of us has turned to our own way. And Yahweh has laid on Him the sin of us all.' Isaiah said that the Servant would be like a lamb led to be sacrificed. He wouldn't fight back or complain. Who was this Servant? About seven hundred years later, Jesus died on a cross. He was rejected, He suffered, and He took the punishment for our sins, just as Isaiah said. Jesus took our place, so we could be forgiven and have peace with God. And three days later, Jesus rose again! This is the best news in the whole world. Jesus loves you so much that He took your place.

memory_verse.text: The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

identity_focus.core_truth: Jesus took my place, so I am forgiven and have peace with God.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: Isaiah said, 'All of us, like sheep, have wandered away.' Jesus came to bring us back. How does it feel to know Jesus took your place?

quiz.question: How did Isaiah describe the Servant?
options: Despised, rejected, and a man of sorrows
quiz.explanation: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease.

quiz.question: What does Isaiah say about the Servant's wounds?
options: By His wounds we are healed
quiz.explanation: By his wounds we are healed.

quiz.question: Who fulfilled Isaiah's words about the Suffering Servant?
quiz.explanation: The apostles taught that Jesus fulfilled Isaiah 53 when He died for our sins and rose again.

micro_prayer.text: Jesus, thank You for taking my place. You were wounded so I could be healed and forgiven. I love You, and I'm so thankful for what You did for me. Amen.

companion.message: Isaiah wrote these words long before Jesus came. When I read them now, I'm amazed. God's rescue plan was always about Jesus taking our place.

review.notes: Isaiah 53 is read Christologically (as the apostles did in Acts 8). Crucifixion imagery is kept minimal; no suffering depicted. Confirm framing.
